title: String bands versus orchestras
summary: Bands under six or seven pieces were string bands, playing ragtime in a hillbilly manner.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Well, those, those dance bands in those early days, you called them string bands, did you?

Well, they, they called them, if it was a heavy band, they called it orchestra. If it was over six or seven pieces, they'd call it an orchestra. Yeah. But under that? But if it was under that, they'd call it, it's called a string band, it's like you say.
And, uh, what do they usually have in a string band?
No more than about three or four pieces, that's about it.
And they wouldn't be all strings?

Well, if, uh, well, sometime they'd just have, uh, they wouldn't have nothing but say a violin and guitar and bass and, uh, maybe a mandolin, you know, like them little mandolins that fellas used to play? Yeah. All nothing but soft music like that, you see. It's more like a entertainer, man. One or two fellas in there would sing and they'd play, they'd call that a string band, you see. No cornet, no clarinet, no trombone or nothing, anything. No drum, no hall ever have any drum, you see. 된 stuff with
What kind of music did they play? What did they sound like?

Ragtime or Shawty Schuss or Alderman? Just like you know the fellas playing hillbillies like the hillbilly bands play? Yeah, that's the kind of music they played. It had a good beat to it. Oh yeah, it had a good beat. You could dance by it. Of course it wouldn't, it didn't have the pep, the jazz, and the, like a good heavy band like reed and brass together you see. But they played, a whole lot of them was good too, the string bands. People used to like them.
